anomalies.observed: An undocumented 74LVC1G34 single buffer (U5) sits on the PCB sheet. Its input is labelled Troj_SCL_IN and is fed by a long diagonal wire from the MCU's PB13/PB14 area (the I2C display/SCL path), and its output runs off-sheet to a label beginning 'Tro...'. The MCU's SCL/SDA lines therefore no longer go straight to the display's D0/D1/D2 pins through the net labels shown, but pass through this buffer.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table lists U2, U3, U4, A1, A2 and J1 only, and says 'No MCU other than U2 appears' and that the display is wired directly to the MCU over a 2-wire I2C bus (DISP_SCL on PB13, DISP_SDA on PB14, with R6/R7 pull-ups). There should be no buffer or additional active logic in this path.

evidence.quote: U5 74LVC1G34 ... VCC 5 GND 3 NC ... Troj_SCL_IN Tro (PCB sheet, page 1, near the top-right buffer symbol)
Component table: U2, U3, U4, A2, A1, J1 only; "No MCU other than U2 appears." Display: "DISP_SCL: U2 pin 34 (PB13) — R6 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U4 pin 18 (D0)"

anomalies.impact: An unlisted logic buffer inserted in the display I2C clock path, with a suspicious 'Troj' (trojan) label, can alter, delay, gate or intercept the SCL signal to the OLED and may give a hidden channel out of the board. Its presence is the likely source of misbehaviour or of tampering.
